predecessors.name: Mali Empire
predecessors.text: the Wolof country, a vassal of Mali "for much of its" earlier history; permanent independence c.

successors.name: Jolof Kingdom
successors.text: the Jolof heartland around Linguère (the Louga region)

successors.name: Baol
successors.text: Baol left the empire after Danki

successors.name: Waalo
successors.text: Waalo, the northern tributary state on the lower Senegal river

ledger.x: c. 1360: Jolof becomes an independent empire under the buurba. "Ogot dates permanent independence from Mali to a succession dispute c. 1360"; the infobox says "Established c. 1360"; the founder is "possibly mythical" Ndiadiane Ndiaye.
early: Cayor and Baol are absorbed.
Waalo is a tributary of Jolof: "Northern core state, tributary to Jolof" (no year).
late 14th century: Sine becomes a tributary of Jolof.

c. 1450s: Biram Njeme Eler conquers Namandirou and then extends his authority over Takrur. Jolof page: "conquered Namandirou in approximately the 1450s, then extended his authority over Takrur"; 1455 is a bridging year inside the page's decade. [Fix af-03-x 2026-10-19: counterpart was 'takrur', a dossier that…

c. 1450s: the Gambia states are subdued. "Gambia states (Niumi, Baddibu, Nyani, Wuli): subdued by Eler (c. 1450s) as the Mali Empire declined." Jolof page (re-read 2026-10-19): Eler was "likely responsible for subduing the Mandinka states on the northern bank of the Gambia, including Niumi, Baddibu, Nyani, and Wuli…
1549: Waalo leaves the empire after Danki.
1549: Wuli and Niani, Gambian states, leave Jolof after Danki (the Danki page names them).

wars.name: Battle of Danki
wars.outcome: Cayor, under crown prince Amari Ngoone Sobel Fall, defeated Jolof near Lake Danki, the buurba Léléfoulifak was killed and Cayor, Baol, Saloum, Sine, Wuli, Niani and Waalo left the empire; Amary "fought off several attempts by succeeding buurbas to reassert…

wars.name: Koli Tenguella's conquest of Futa Toro
wars.outcome: Koli Tenguella seized Futa Toro from Jolof in 1513 with a Fulani and Mandinka force.

certainty.note: The pages name no frontier; the empire was a core with tributary states.
